messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: sev2 - hosted-api us-east-1 high queue growth detected. p95 spike to 6.3s, p99 to 22s, queue +18k in 5m. paging maya and oncall SREs.
maya: I'm oncall, seeing the alerts. dashboards show sustained enqueue rate ~3.2k/s. trying to pull autoscaler logs now.
liam: looking at autoscaler. I see a lot of 'InstanceProvisionError: quota exceeded' when trying to scale GPU pool. provisioning stuck at 0 -> 12 for several groups.
jordan: runtime confirms KV-cache pressure low, but worker pods stuck in provisioning. no recent runtime deploys.
anna: support: two paying customers reported intermittent 504s ~5m ago. their traffic patterns are heavy beam tests. flagged as potentially contributing.
liam: provider console shows quota error on GPU instance quota for project-redwood-us-east. requests are being throttled by cloud. autoscaler keeps retrying but fails with 403/Quota.
maya: ok mitigation plan: 1) route new requests over to eu-west and dedicated-overflow where possible, 2) enable emergency soft-throttle (20%) to shed experimental clients, 3) reduce default max_tokens to 512 for hosted tier temporarily. who can flip routing?
jordan: I can flip a weighted routing rule for compatible models. pushing a runtime rule to prefer dedicated-overflow for requests with tokens>1024. doing a dry-run first.
liam: I'll attempt to increase instance quota request with cloud console but that takes time. also triggering quick firmware: restart autoscaler control-plane to clear stuck operations (will cause short blip in scale decisions).
maya: @deploy-bot can you annotate the change and the exact command used? we need audit trail.
deploy-bot: annotate: routing-weight update by jordan at 2456789027. Command: 
```
redwood route update --region us-east-1 --model all --prefer-pool dedicated-overflow --weight 0.6
```
jordan: toggled the routing weight to 0.6 for dedicated-overflow for large-token requests. monitoring now.
liam: restarting autoscaler controller: 
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller
kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler-controller -f --since=2m
```
liam: after restart autoscaler shows reduced provisioning retries and API now returns fewer quota errors; however we still can't provision new GPUs due to cloud quota.
maya: how's queue length?
jordan: queue growth rate dropped from +18k/5m -> +3k/10m after routing and restart. p95 improved to 2.1s, p99 to 9.6s. still elevated but trending down.
anna: support: notifying affected customers with the mitigation steps and ETA. copy: "We're routing traffic to overflow pools and applying throttles; you may see reduced throughput for high-concurrency tests. Engineers are working on permanent capacity"
liam: temporary token cap applied: 512 for hosted API. Config patch: 
```
PATCH /config/runtime
{"hosted.default_max_tokens":512}
```
maya: also enabling request-shed for unrated API keys: 
```
redwood limiter update --policy emergency-shed --threshold 2000 --drop-rate 0.2
```
jordan: monitoring shows fewer new huge requests after shed. flashbacks of backpressure from edge are calmer.
liam: submitted quota increase request to cloud: ticket CLOUD-98765, asked for +40 GPU instances. ETA unknown. opened temporary manual override for provisioning to try different instance types (lower-capacity GPUs) to bypass quota.
maya: note: that override can change perf; only use if necessary. document in incident ticket.
liam: switching a subset of queued new requests to smaller-quantized model variant (ql-8bit) to reduce GPU memory footprint. Doing a canary to 5% of traffic.
jordan: canary seems fine, latency for canary path p95 ~1.8s.
anna: raising support severity to customers affected, giving ETA "monitoring for stabilization in 15-30m, follow-ups to come".
maya: handoff plan: I'll stay for the next 20m while we verify stabilization, then hand to liam for overnight watch and post-incident writeup. create incident ticket INC-24567 with timeline, mitigation steps, and customer list.
liam: acknowledging handoff. action items: 1) track quota ticket, 2) remove emergency throttles after stabilized, 3) run span test to verify no regressions.
maya: quick note for retrospective: consider an automated fallback that routes >90th percentile token requests to dedicated-overflow automatically when provisioning errors detected. also add alert to correlate provider quota errors to autoscaler failures.
jordan: agreed. add to eng-runtime backlog.
anna: customers notified, some already reduced their tests; support will follow up with any escalations.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue length stabilized to +2k over baseline, p95 1.9s, p99 7.4s. status: mitigation in progress.
maya: closing paging loop now. handoff to liam at 2456789090. I'll file notes in INC-24567 and create follow-up action items. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
